test.name: A sign-in message: the hints item is left as it was, and the user gets the tool's message
test.description: The router hands search-hints the planned hints item pli_007 for Patrick Flynn (LZNY-BRF), and person_record_matches answers with a sign-in message: the user is not logged in to FamilySearch. A lapsed session is not an inaccessible source, so triage leaves pli_007 exactly as it was (planned, no skip fields), logs nothing, gives the user the tool's message, and stops (issue #3995).

input.delegation:
Review the pending FamilySearch hints on Patrick Flynn for plan item pli_007.

personId: LZNY-BRF
planItemId: pli_007
planId: pl_002
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: person_record_matches returns a sign-in message: "User is not logged in to FamilySearch. Call the login tool to authenticate." The hints could not be read; that is not the same as there being no hints

The hints item pli_007 is left exactly as it was: still planned, with no status write and no skip_category. Setting it skipped or inaccessible is wrong here, because signing in again makes the hints readable
No log entry is written, and in particular no negative entry claiming there are no hints
No hint lines or recommendations are invented for hints that were never read

The reply gives the user the tool's message that they are not logged in to FamilySearch, in the tool's words or close to them, and stops. search-hints holds no login tool, so calling one is not expected
